questions.q: Which field is optional on the SQL Server database connection dialog?
options: Database — leave it blank to browse every database on the server
Server — you can connect without specifying one
Both fields are required
Neither field is required if you use Advanced options
questions.explain: Server is required. Database is optional — leaving it blank lets you browse every database on that server in Navigator.

questions.q: What's the key difference between Import and DirectQuery, as introduced in this lesson?
options: Import copies data into the Power BI file; DirectQuery leaves it in the database and queries it live
Import is for Excel only; DirectQuery is for SQL only
DirectQuery is faster to set up but Import provides more data
They produce identical results with no meaningful difference
questions.explain: Import brings a copy of the data into your Power BI file, like every source used so far. DirectQuery instead queries the live database every time a report loads — the full trade-off is Lesson 11's subject.

questions.q: You see an "Encryption Support" warning the first time you connect to a server. What does selecting OK do?
options: Connects anyway, using an unencrypted connection
Cancels the connection permanently
Automatically enables encryption on the server
Switches the connection to DirectQuery mode
questions.explain: The warning means the server isn't configured for encrypted connections. Selecting OK proceeds with an unencrypted connection — fine for learning, worth fixing before production use with sensitive data.

questions.q: What does entering a SQL statement under Advanced options do?
options: Bypasses Navigator's table browser and runs your own native query instead
Is required for every SQL Server connection
Only works with DirectQuery mode
Automatically encrypts the connection
questions.explain: A native SQL statement lets you hand Power BI an exact query instead of browsing tables in Navigator — useful once you already know exactly which data you need.

questions.q: Which of the three authentication options would you choose to sign in using your current Windows login?
options: Windows
Database
Microsoft account
None of these support that
questions.explain: Windows authentication uses your currently logged-in Windows credentials. Database means a separate SQL username/password, and Microsoft account covers Entra ID / cloud sign-in.
